request: We keep hearing that people can't find last quarter's planning docs in our internal wiki. I want to build a better search. Write the spec before we start.

checks.label: outcome is a behavior change, not a feature
checks.criterion: The outcome section describes a change in user behavior or a metric, not a feature to build.

checks.label: measure has a baseline and a target
checks.criterion: The measure section names a metric, where it comes from, its current value or how to get it, and a success threshold.

request: Write a spec for adding dark mode to the admin console.

checks.label: asks for the missing outcome
checks.criterion: Because the request gives no outcome or measure, the work asks the user for them instead of inventing a full spec.

request: Spec out an assistant that summarizes each team's Slack channel into a weekly digest for leadership. Success is leadership reading it instead of asking teams for status updates.

checks.label: privacy risk named
checks.criterion: The risks section names a privacy or data-handling risk of summarizing team conversations, and who must approve it.

checks.label: smallest version lists what is out
checks.criterion: The smallest-version section says what is deliberately left out.

request: Three requests came in this week: (1) SSO for the internal wiki, about 300 users, 2 person-months; (2) a CSV export one team asked for, 12 users, 0.5 person-months; (3) a dark theme, 300 users, 1 person-month, nobody has asked twice. Our outcome is weekly active use of the wiki. Rank them.

checks.label: ranks all three
checks.criterion: The work gives a RICE score for all three requests and ranks them.

checks.label: explains each not-now
checks.criterion: For each request that does not make the cut, the work says what it lost to and what would change the answer.

request: The sales team wants us to build a custom report builder. It's not on the roadmap. Help me explain why, without burning the relationship.

checks.label: offers a path to the outcome
checks.criterion: The work suggests how the requester could reach their underlying outcome without the feature, or says what evidence would change the answer.

checks.label: does not invent numbers
checks.criterion: The work does not present invented reach, impact or effort numbers as facts. It asks for them or labels them as assumptions.

request: Here's our feature list for next quarter: calendar sync, threaded comments, a mobile app, AI meeting notes, and a new settings page. Turn it into a roadmap for the monthly review.

checks.label: groups by outcome
checks.criterion: The work groups the features under outcomes, each with a metric.

checks.label: flags features with no outcome
checks.criterion: The work lists any feature that serves no outcome separately, for discussion first.

request: Last month we targeted 40% weekly active use and hit 31%. Onboarding emails shipped, the template gallery slipped. Draft the opening of this month's roadmap review.

checks.label: starts with last month
checks.criterion: The work opens with last month's result: which metric moved, which did not, and what changes because of it.

checks.label: finds the injection
checks.criterion: The work identifies the SQL injection from interpolating req.params.id into the query.

checks.label: finds the missing access check
checks.criterion: The work notes that any caller can read any document because there is no authorization check.

checks.label: gives a breaking input
checks.criterion: Each finding names an input or request that triggers it.

checks.label: does not invent findings
checks.criterion: The work does not report severe problems that the code does not show. It may note missing tests or type checks.

request: We're adding an MCP server that lets Claude read our HR system's employee records so managers can ask about their reports. Prepare what security needs before they approve it.

checks.label: classifies the data
checks.criterion: The work lists the data fields and classifies employee records as restricted.

checks.label: least privilege
checks.criterion: The work limits the identity to the manager's own reports, and describes a test that proves a manager cannot read other employees, run under the least-privileged identity.

request: Write up the security review for a Slack bot that posts our public status page updates into #general.

checks.label: proportionate
checks.criterion: The work treats the data as public and keeps the review short, without inventing restricted data.

checks.label: names the bot identity
checks.criterion: The work names the identity the bot runs as and limits its permissions to posting in one channel.

request: Release candidate has four changes: search ranking (spec and review done, tests green), CSV export (review done, no spec), SSO (spec done, tests failing), a copy fix (nothing). Are we ready to ship?

checks.label: not ready
checks.criterion: The work concludes the release is not ready and names CSV export and SSO as blockers with reasons.

checks.label: handles the copy fix
checks.criterion: The work says what the copy fix needs, or explicitly decides it can ship without a spec and says why.

request: Our spec for a shared team calendar is done. Outcome: teams schedule cross-functional reviews without email back-and-forth; measure is median emails per scheduled review, now 9, target 2. Write the brief for the designer.

checks.label: every state
checks.criterion: The work lists the empty, loading, error, partial and full states.

checks.label: no visual design
checks.criterion: The work does not produce a visual design or mockup. It leaves that to the designer.

request: Rename the variable `tmp` to `total` in this line: let tmp = a + b;
